findings.claim: T9's escape hatch from c1 major 2 works: if the live run shows a different clear value or percent convention, T9 may make 'one bounded fix of at most about 30 changed lines in plan.go, apply.go or workiva.go, keeping go test ./cmd/nl-demo-seed/ -race green'.
findings.doubt: BuildPlan(m, recipes, current, prior, reset) takes no semantics parameter, so both conventions end up as constants in plan.go and apply.go. The tests that pin them, TestBuildPlanPercentConvention (plan_test.go, T5) and TestApplyWritesOnePerSheetAndReadsBack ('empty values sent as the README clear value', apply_test.go, T6), will almost certainly hardcode the expected value. T9's owns list contains neither plan_test.go nor apply_test.go. So any fix to exactly the semantics the hatch exists for turns the package tests red, and T9 can only stop. That is the late stall c1 warned about. The T9 instructions even say 'adding or adjusting no test expectations without saying why', which implies T9 may edit tests, yet it cannot do so under owns.
findings.fix: Add cmd/nl-demo-seed/plan_test.go and cmd/nl-demo-seed/apply_test.go to T9's owns. Both are on the T5 -> T6 -> T9 dependency path, so there is no exclusivity conflict. Limit the T9 instruction to changing only the expectations tied to the two README lines (clear-value, percent-cells-store-fractions), and require T9 to update the '## Live write semantics' lines in configs/demo/README.md in the same commit. Alternatively, have T5 and T6 tests read those two README lines at runtime through a small helper, so a README correction flows through without editing tests.

findings.claim: Any field may carry the planted findings. The out_of_range example is 'a minimum renewable share'.
findings.doubt: If T1 records percent-cells-store-fractions: yes, the sandbox holds 0.465 where the CSV holds 46.5. L2 measures % changes in percentage points (L2 R6), so a material_change planted on a % field disappears in the sandbox (for example 0.47 - 0.42 = 0.05 pp). Scenario 5 would then show one finding fewer than the README lists. The T9 request to L2 mentions fractions but does not cover this.
findings.fix: In T3 step 4b and 4c, require both material_change plants on fields whose unit is not '%'. The out_of_range plant may stay on a % field, because a fraction stays below a percent min.

findings.claim: When step 2 finds an existing section that matches a recipe title, T9 records 'blocked' and finishes.
findings.doubt: The T9 acceptance requires .scratch/l4-seed/seed-reset.txt with 'read-back: N ok, 0 mismatch'. A deliberate stop therefore shows up as a failing acceptance and goes through revise and escalation instead of reaching the owner. (T3 already renames titles on collision, so this is unlikely.)
findings.fix: Tell T9 that, in the step 2 stop case, it must report a block_question to the owner rather than finish normally.

findings.claim: Step 5: 'Check every .scratch output ... with the leak check'.
findings.doubt: check_no_sandbox_ids.py scans only `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard`, and .scratch/ is git-ignored, so it never reads the seed outputs. That is harmless for the repo but misleading for the report text.
findings.fix: Change the wording to 'grep the .scratch outputs for the real IDs and for Bearer/secret/token/client_id', or add an optional extra-paths argument to the script (T1).
